clue.text: Diplomat attacked intrigues

blocks.note: to charge is to rush at in attack
affaires is the French-flavoured spelling of affairs, illicit liaisons or intrigues

explanation.surface: An envoy has been set upon by schemers at court.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARGE D'AFFAIRES is a French phrase, so the second half keeps its French spelling with the extra E.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargé d'affaires is an embassy official standing in for an absent ambassador, so a kind of diplomat.

clue.text: Correct, neat, trim - he's a hard taskmaster

indicators.note: to correct something is to put it right, so the following letters are rearranged into proper order

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone who insists everything be correct, neat and trim sounds like a demanding boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct, neat, trim' reads as a list of the boss's demands, but the first word is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian who insists on rules being obeyed, named after a French army drillmaster.

clue.text: Finally nails Conservative lie

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the end of nails
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: At last a Tory politician is caught out in a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: A story is an informal word for a falsehood, as a child is told not to tell stories.

clue.text: Mist hung about Winchester?

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around, out of their printed order

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Fog hangs over the cathedral city of Winchester in Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester looks like the English city, but the question mark flags it as the American firearms maker of the Winchester rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester company made rifles, so it is an example of a firearms maker, defined by example with a question mark.

clue.text: Public workers' group makes agreement about first of strikes

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the next word
about here means going around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a union is a coming together, an agreement
the opening letter of strikes

explanation.surface: A trade union reaches a deal after the first walkouts.
explanation.walkthrough: UNISON is the large British trade union for public-sector workers; the union around S builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is the name of Britain's main trade union for staff in public services such as health and local government.

clue.text: Island attracts mostly stale bunch of stars

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the Italian island in the Bay of Naples
corny means trite or stale, as a joke

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean island draws a tired crowd of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities on Capri, but here it means the stars in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is a zodiac constellation, a group of stars imagined as a goat.

clue.text: Singer, 51, at festival

blocks.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A 51-year-old singer performs at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The number reads as the singer's age, but it is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Divali, also spelt Diwali, is the Hindu festival of lights held in autumn.

clue.text: Ann Hindle, terror suspect in Ulster

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not as it seems, so its letters are not in true order

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A woman named Ann Hindle is held as a terrorism suspect in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as a noun describing the woman, but it is an adjective signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is the traditional name commonly used for the six counties forming Northern Ireland within the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Ben and Arthur ill with indigestion

indicators.note: ill means unwell or in a bad state, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the two names taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Two men, Ben and Arthur, are laid up with stomach trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartburn is a burning pain in the chest caused by acid reflux, a common symptom of indigestion.

clue.text: Miami godfather shields pal

indicators.note: to shield is to hold something inside and protect it, so the words conceal a run of letters

blocks.note: spanning the end of the city and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A Florida mob boss protects his friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English for a mate or buddy.

clue.text: Hands back profits

blocks.note: first meaning: gives something back to its owner
second meaning: yields from an investment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands back' looks like a phrase about body parts, but the verb sense is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns is both a verb for giving things back and a noun for the income earned on an investment.

clue.text: Employee emerging from rough taverns

indicators.note: rough means crude or unpolished, so the word's letters are roughly rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A worker comes out of some seedy pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is a person employed to do work for someone else, especially household duties.

clue.text: One's lost for ages

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: the word without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone's been missing for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For ages' sounds like part of the story, but 'for' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are immensely long stretches of time, and the plural matches ages used loosely for a long while.

clue.text: I get a nice long cocktail, which makes my mouth numb!

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a tall drink and finds it numbs their mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail' looks like the drink, but it is the anagram signal for the other words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lignocaine, also called lidocaine, is a local anaesthetic dentists inject to deaden feeling in the gums.

clue.text: Shortens agreements

blocks.note: first meaning: makes smaller or tighter
second meaning: binding legal documents

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for drawing together or shrinking and a plural noun for formal binding deals.

clue.text: To China's ruined ancient city

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters lie broken and rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A trip to China takes in a ruined city of antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition; Antioch is not in China at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a great city of the ancient Greek and Roman world, in what is now southern Turkey.

clue.text: Queen is surrounded by entourage in the country

indicators.note: being surrounded means sitting inside something else, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a train is a retinue of followers
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A queen travelling in the countryside is hemmed in by her retinue.
explanation.definitionFit: Country in the sense of land or ground, as in hilly country, is a synonym for terrain.

clue.text: Insensitive and without skill?

blocks.note: first meaning: thoughtless about others' feelings
second, playful meaning: lacking tact, taking tact as a skill in handling people

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning splits the word into tact plus a suffix meaning without.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactless describes someone clumsy with feelings; tact is the diplomatic skill such a person lacks.

clue.text: A compound discovered in minor planet

blocks.note: taken as written
a steroid is a type of organic chemical compound

explanation.surface: Scientists find a chemical on a small planet.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, which astronomers also call a minor planet.

clue.text: Leading judges and senior politicians

blocks.note: in front means leading
the bench is the collective term for judges

explanation.surface: Top judges and top politicians are listed together.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK the front bench means government ministers and their opposition shadows, who sit on the front benches of the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: The front bench is the group of ministers and shadow ministers, the most senior members of parliament.

clue.text: Ring doctor to attend home birth

blocks.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O
to doctor or rig something is to tamper with it
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone calls a doctor to be present at a home birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring doctor' reads as phoning the doctor, but both words are pieces and the doctor is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Birth in the sense of beginnings or descent, as in of humble birth, matches origin.

clue.text: Force us to leave Guernsey, unfortunately

indicators.note: the pronoun is told to leave, so its letters are taken out of the island's name
unfortunately signals things going badly wrong, so what remains is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be removed
the Channel Island taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone laments being forced off the island of Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: Guernsey is one of the Channel Islands; take a U and an S from it and rearrange the remaining six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Force and energy are near-synonyms for power or vigour, as in the force or energy of a blow.

clue.text: Leaders of subversive tendency incite revolution and disorder

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Radical agitators stoke up revolt and chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or public disturbance, a fair synonym for disorder in the sense of unrest.

clue.text: Punishment for some garrulous Trappists

indicators.note: some means a part only, so a portion of the following words is taken

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Chatty monks of a silent order deserve a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Trappists are monks who keep a vow of silence, which is the joke of garrulous ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The strap was a leather belt once used to beat schoolchildren, so the word stands for that punishment.

clue.text: Copy information initially, then get it into China

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
getting something into another thing places it inside, so one piece goes within the next

blocks.note: the opening letter of information
taken as written
china is rhyming slang for mate: china plate, mate

explanation.surface: Instructions for copying data and getting it into China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a friend. 'China' looks like the country, but it is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone's actions or style is to imitate them, an everyday synonym for mimicking.

clue.text: Shoot dead three fifths of those in rally

indicators.note: three fifths asks for three letters out of five, here the opening run of the word

blocks.note: the late means the dead
the opening three of its five letters

explanation.surface: A gunman opens fire, killing several people at a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' reads as a verb about firing a gun, but it is a botanical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a lateral is a side shoot growing from a main stem, so a shoot is a fair definition.

clue.text: Poet and priest love to talk at first

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest, a crossword regular
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the opening letter of talk

explanation.surface: A poet and a clergyman are keen to chat first.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot was the American-born British poet who wrote The Waste Land.

clue.text: Awkward age in tot's development

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy and ungainly, so the letters stumble into a new order

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A toddler goes through a difficult phase as they grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is the development of a baby in the womb, and figuratively the slow growth of an idea.
